# Tier-2 Dependencies - Require Manual Review Before Merge
#
# Criteria (any match triggers tier-2):
# - New direct dependencies (not transitive)
# - Handles: network/IO, cryptography, unsafe code, financial data
# - Repo signals: <100 GitHub stars, unmaintained (>1yr), single maintainer
#
# Format:
#   crate           - tier-2, any version change needs review
#   crate=x.y.z     - PINNED, exact version required
#
# Pinned entries include: # review-date | risk-factors
# The auto-merge workflow reads this file and applies 'tier-2' label.
# The "tier-2 pins" CI job (.github/scripts/check-tier2-pins.sh) enforces that every PINNED
# entry above matches the `=` requirement in every manifest declaring that crate, so a bump
# cannot land while leaving this record behind. CI cannot verify that the re-verification a
# pinned entry mandates was actually performed — only that this file was not left untouched.

ibapi=3.3.0  # 2026-09-14 | Financial protocol, community-maintained, no official SDK. Reviewed 3.2.0->3.3.0, all four properties recorded at 3.2.0 re-verified and still hold: zero unsafe (also no transmute/from_raw/extern "C"/asm!; holds by inspection, not by lint — upstream has no #![forbid(unsafe_code)]), no build.rs, dependency tree byte-identical vs 3.2.0 (both Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock differ by the version line alone; 9 direct deps under our `default-features = false, features = ["sync"]` selection, unchanged), still only a caller-supplied TWS socket (reconnect reuses the caller's address — no fallback host, no telemetry) + the opt-in local recorder dir (IBAPI_RECORDING_DIR; recorder.rs byte-identical). Env set unchanged (IBAPI_RECORDING_DIR, IBAPI_TIMEZONE_ALIASES); no process spawn, no obfuscation; published from git b140b312d1136d240f3b5651a89f4778e01aa222.
#   New in 3.3.0, reviewed: `src/config` — despite the name it reads NO local files and NO env vars. It wraps two TWS wire messages (ReqConfig=108/UpdateConfig=109) over the already-open socket, whose protobuf types already existed in 3.2.0. Version-gated, #[must_use] builder, not reachable during connect/handshake.
#   NOTE (capability, not vulnerability): `update_config()` can write the gateway's own safety settings — read_only_api, the bypass_* order precautions, trusted_ips, allow_localhost_only, socket_port, master_client_id. rustrade does not call it and does not re-export it; keep it out of the wrapper surface unless there is a deliberate reason.
#   Upstream BREAKING in a minor release: the `fundamental` module was removed (IBKR retired reqFundamentalData in TWS API 10.47). rustrade never used it — verified no reference to fundamental_data / FundamentalData / FundamentalReportType / TickType::FundamentalRatios.
#   The serde-xml-rs/xml-rs note at rustrade-data/Cargo.toml is UNCHANGED and still accurate: they are build-deps of time-tz (non-optional dep of ibapi, timezone codegen), single path each, never linked into the binary. Removing `fundamental` did not and could not drop them — ibapi never had a direct XML dependency.
#   ORDER WIRE FORMAT audited (3.x places orders via protobuf only, so the proto path IS the order wire): the entire encoder delta is 2 lines — `hedge_max_size` (new tag 144) and `deactivate`. Both go through `some_bool`/Option, which omit the field on the default value, so the bytes sent for any order rustrade builds today are byte-identical to 3.2.0. market_data/contracts encoders are byte-identical.
#   3.3.0 rolls up 3.2.1's transport rework, which is NOT fully described in the upstream changelog. Request-less TWS errors (id == -1) outside the 2100..=2169 warning range — which includes the connectivity codes 1100/1101/1102/1300 — now fail in-flight one-shot requests instead of hanging, and the sync shared-queue drain in `send_shared_request` makes concurrent callers of the SAME one-shot API able to discard each other's response. NEITHER REACHES US: rustrade calls none of the affected one-shot APIs (next_valid_order_id, managed_accounts, server_time, family_codes, market_rule, market_depth_exchanges, news_providers, scanner_parameters, wsh_metadata). `client.next_order_id()` is a different method — a local counter increment, byte-identical across the two versions, not a request. Re-check this if the wrapper ever starts calling one of those.
#   NOT VERIFIABLE OFF-GATEWAY: the handshake now advertises server version 225 (was 221), so a modern TWS may negotiate the 222/224 field layouts. No decoder branches on them. The ibkr integration tests are all #[ignore]d (they need a live TWS), so this bump has NOT been exercised against a real gateway — do that before relying on it in production.
#   Other additive breaks that cost us nothing, verified: TickType gained 6 odd-lot variants and lost FundamentalRatios=47 (explicit discriminants, so no renumbering; our quotes.rs matches use `_` fallbacks), and `Order` gained 2 public fields (we build orders with `..Order::default()`).
binance-sdk=69.1.0  # 2026-09-14 | Exchange SDK, signing/IO. PINNED: margin user-data stream couples to 3 `binance_sdk::common` internals (lower-stability than the public per-market API). ANY bump MUST re-verify all 3 before merge:
#   1. common::websocket::WebsocketApi::send_message      — signature + WebsocketMessageSendOptions signing fields (margin WS subscribe send)
#   2. ws.common.events.subscribe (WebsocketEventEmitter) — receive/event-callback path (margin WS event delivery)
#   3. common::utils::send_request                        — signature + HMAC signing + X-MBX-APIKEY header (hand-rolled `userListenToken` POST; SDK binds no endpoint for it)
# Background: legacy margin listen-key user-data API retired 2026-02-20; SDK binds only the dead endpoint, so the live `userListenToken` flow is hand-rolled atop these internals.
#
# Re-verified against the vendored =69.1.0 source on 2026-09-14 (60.0.0 -> 69.1.0, nine majors). All 3 still hold,
# and the strongest evidence is that they cannot have changed: `common/websocket.rs` is BYTE-IDENTICAL between
# 60.0.0 and 69.1.0 (md5 38b5990bb85497fdbcec39984732509b), as are common/{mod,config,models}.rs. The only file
# that differs in `common/` is utils.rs, and its entire delta is `build_user_agent` plus that function's tests.
#   1. `send_message(&self, method: &str, payload: BTreeMap<String, Value>,
#      options: WebsocketMessageSendOptions) -> Result<SendWebsocketMessageResult<R>, WebsocketError>`
#      — shape unchanged (websocket.rs:1630); WebsocketMessageSendOptions still carries exactly
#      with_api_key / is_signed / is_session_logon / is_session_logout. Both margin WS call sites still match.
#   2. `WebsocketEventEmitter::subscribe` (websocket.rs:125) still spawns exactly one task per subscription
#      draining an unbounded channel via a sequential `while let Some(event) = rx.recv().await` loop, so the
#      FnMut is invoked sequentially. That is precisely the contract the non-atomic `Option::take()`
#      in the margin `account_stream` callback relies on for soundness.
#   3. `send_request(configuration, endpoint, method, query_params, body_params, time_unit, is_signed)`
#      — 7-arg shape unchanged (utils.rs:841); `is_signed` still injects `timestamp` (:857-858), signs via
#      `configuration.signature_gen.get_signature(...)` (:866-870), appends `signature` to the query string
#      (:887-889), and sets `X-MBX-APIKEY` (:923-925). The hand-rolled `POST /sapi/v1/userListenToken` is
#      therefore still signed as intended.
#
# Dependency surface: `[dependencies]`, `[dev-dependencies]` and `[build-dependencies]` are byte-for-byte
# identical across all nine majors. The only manifest change is the removal of the `nft` feature (30 -> 29);
# `spot` and `margin_trading` are unchanged and still mean the same thing. No new or removed deps, no MSRV
# change (neither version declares `rust-version`), no new duplicate majors, `anyhow` still the public error
# type. build.rs is identical (6 lines, stamps RUSTC_VERSION). The version number tracks Binance's REST
# surface, not dependency churn — which is why nine majors cost nothing here.
#
# Security: PASS. 60.0.0 has 0 `unsafe`; 69.1.0 has 10, ALL inside `#[cfg(test)]` (utils.rs:1382-1432,
# `env::set_var`/`remove_var`, which edition 2024 requires be wrapped in `unsafe`). Credentials: hand-written
# REDACTING `Debug` on every secret-bearing struct, zero `Serialize` in config.rs. Network hosts: one added
# (`wss://nbstream.binance.com`, behind the `alpha` feature, which we do not enable), one removed (NFT).
# Filesystem: one `read_to_string` of the caller's own PEM. No process exec, no obfuscation. Publisher
# unchanged. Git commits: 60.0.0 = 8cfe7d023236280e9356f84a8c4a12eff558d4aa,
# 69.1.0 = 56a82d787bfc0fc5e321691fdfdbe2b6767f1f0b.
#
# Two findings recorded, neither blocking, both worth knowing before enabling verbose tracing:
#   a. NEW env read `BINANCE_CONNECTOR_RUST_USER_AGENT` (utils.rs:395), regex-gated to binance-cli/binance-skill
#      shapes. The `[^;()]+` character classes admit \r and \n, and the resulting UA is applied via
#      `.parse().unwrap()` (utils.rs:921) — so a crafted value PANICS on HeaderValue parse. That is a DoS, not
#      header injection, and it requires control of the process environment. We never set this variable.
#   b. PRE-EXISTING and NOT a regression (identical in both versions): websocket.rs:1665 logs
#      `debug!("Sending message to WebSocket API: {:?}", request)` — the full signed WS request INCLUDING
#      `apiKey` and `signature` — at DEBUG level. `api_secret` is never logged. Anything enabling DEBUG tracing
#      for this crate will put short-lived credentials in its logs.
#
# Consumer-side API churn this bump required (recorded so the next bump knows the shape): binance-sdk now
# generates a typed enum per endpoint parameter where it used to take `String` (`isIsolated`, order `type`,
# `sideEffectType`), and a distinct response struct per endpoint where `allOrders` and `openOrders` used to
# share one. The enums are wire-identical to the strings they replace (`TRUE`/`FALSE`, `LIMIT`, ...), so the
# migration is behaviour-preserving; they derive no `PartialEq`, so assertions compare `as_str()`.
#
# Record gap, noted so the shape of the miss is not repeated: this entry read `=52.0.0` until
# 2026-09-13 while the manifest had already moved to `=55.0.0` (aefb55b) and then `=60.0.0` (7d8d081).
# Both were plain Dependabot bumps that changed `rustrade-execution/Cargo.toml` without touching this
# file, so the re-verification this entry mandates was never recorded for either. The 2026-09-13 check
# closed that gap at 60.0.0 and this one carries it forward to 69.1.0. The hard `=` pin in the manifest is
# the enforcement; this file is the record. They must move together, and a bump that edits only the
# manifest has skipped a required step.

quick-xml  # 2026-07-08 | New direct dep (XML parsing of broker Flex statements). Reviewed @ 0.41.0: #![forbid(unsafe_code)] crate-wide, zero net-new transitive deps (serde+memchr only, both already in tree), no RUSTSEC advisories, de-facto-standard parser. Not pinned — any version bump still needs review.
#   Re-reviewed @ 0.42.0 (2026-09-16), the review this entry's "any version bump still needs
#   review" mandates. All four properties recorded at 0.41.0 re-verified and still hold:
#   `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` is still crate-wide (the 9 `unsafe` occurrences under src/ are all
#   in comments explaining where `get_unchecked`/`unreachable_unchecked` COULD be used and
#   deliberately is not -- zero real unsafe, same count and same sites as 0.41.0); no build.rs in
#   either version; the `[dependencies]` section is byte-identical between the two; and the
#   lockfile delta for this bump is version-only -- 2 lines changed, no package added or removed,
#   so "zero net-new transitive deps (serde+memchr only)" still stands. No RUSTSEC advisories.
#   BREAKING, and the reason this bump needed code: `QName<'a>` changed from `pub &'a [u8]`
#   (name.rs:102) to `pub &'a str` (name.rs:118), and its `AsRef<[u8]>` impl became `AsRef<str>`.
#   That byte->str migration touches most of src/, but our exposure is one line. We take only
#   `features = ["serialize"]` (= serde); `encoding` (= encoding_rs) is NOT enabled, so the
#   non-UTF-8 decoding path this change reworks is not compiled for us at all.
#   Consumer-side change, recorded so the next bump knows the shape: ibkr/flex/mod.rs
#   `root_element_name` dropped its `String::from_utf8_lossy(...)` wrapper. NOT a behaviour
#   change -- that reader is built with `Reader::from_str`, so its input was already guaranteed
#   UTF-8 and the lossy conversion could never have substituted a replacement character. The two
#   `quick_xml::de::from_str` call sites (the serde path, which is the bulk of Flex parsing) are
#   untouched by the QName change.
parquet  # 2026-07-28 | New direct dep (Parquet decode of provider bulk exports). Reviewed @ 59.1.0 and re-verified @ 59.3.0 (2026-09-13), Apache-2.0, apache/arrow-rs (ASF-governed, ~65M downloads). MUST stay `default-features = false, features = ["zstd"]` — that is what keeps `arrow` out, and re-enabling defaults pulls arrow-array/buffer/data/schema/select/ipc, base64, brotli, flate2, lz4, snap and simdutf8 in one line. Under the pinned feature set: no build.rs; no network, process-spawn or env access anywhere in the library (the only `env::var` is in `src/bin/parquet-fromcsv.rs`, a CLI binary we do not build); 19 `unsafe` sites in the compiled paths, all in columnar decode hot spots (bit packing, RLE, byte-stream-split, bloom filter) and idiomatic for the crate class. Tree is 12 direct deps. Net-new surface, measured by diffing Cargo.lock before/after rather than eyeballed: COMPILED ON ORDINARY TARGETS — seq-macro, twox-hash, libm, num-bigint 0.5 (see below), and a second major of ahash (0.8.12, now built alongside the pre-existing 0.7.8). libm is not a new dependency edge: it arrives because parquet's tree turns on the `libm` feature of the already-present num-traits. LOCKFILE-ONLY — const-random and const-random-macro enter Cargo.lock via ahash 0.8 but are target-gated and absent from `cargo tree` on every target we ship; parquet gates ahash's `compile-time-rng` feature (the only thing that pulls const-random) on `cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")`, so they build only for wasm32. Re-check them if this workspace ever targets it -- any downstream consumer targeting wasm32 will compile const-random-macro: const-random-macro is a build-time proc-macro pulling getrandom + tiny-keccak, i.e. a compile-time RNG. ALREADY PRESENT, not new — zstd/zstd-safe/zstd-sys, chrono, bytes, hashbrown, half, num-*, getrandom, once_cell, zerocopy, tiny-keccak. Verified the arrow-free column-reader API compiles and decodes real 4-column and 7-column artifacts (370,531 rows) — the feature reduction is real, not theoretical. 59.2.0 dropped the `paste` dependency outright, which retires the RUSTSEC-2024-0436 exception this entry used to carry: `paste` is no longer in Cargo.lock at all, so there is nothing left to accept. 59.2.0 also moved parquet from num-bigint 0.4 to 0.5 (deps: num-integer + num-traits only, no new surface); 0.4.6 remains in the tree for other consumers, which `bans.multiple-versions = "warn"` permits. 59.3.0 changes the dependency set no further — its list is byte-identical to 59.2.0, and no `arrow-*` crate appears anywhere in Cargo.lock. Not pinned — any version bump still needs review, and must re-check that `arrow` has not become non-optional.
#   UPDATE 2026-09-16: the second ahash major recorded above is gone, and not through anything
#   parquet did. rust_decimal 1.43.0 (#288) dropped its rkyv 0.7 support, which removed rkyv,
#   rkyv_derive, bytecheck, bytecheck_derive, ptr_meta, ptr_meta_derive, rend, seahash and
#   ahash 0.7.8 from Cargo.lock in a single bump -- 9 packages removed, 0 added, verified by
#   diffing the lockfile. parquet still contributes ahash 0.8.12 and that part of the record
#   stands; what is no longer true is "built alongside the pre-existing 0.7.8". 0.8.12 is now
#   the only ahash in the tree, so this entry no longer describes a `bans.multiple-versions`
#   duplicate. Recorded rather than edited in place, because the original sentence was accurate
#   on 2026-07-28 and the value of this file is what was actually reviewed and when. The next
#   parquet bump should re-measure rather than assume either state.
databento  # 2026-09-13 | Direct dep (historical + live market data). Meets the criteria above on three counts — network/IO, credential handling (API key via `DATABENTO_API_KEY`), and financial data — but was never listed when it was introduced; this entry closes that gap rather than recording a new dependency. Reviewed @ 0.61.0, Apache-2.0, databento/databento-rs — a first-party vendor SDK, not community-maintained, which is the opposite of the ibapi risk profile above. No build.rs. Zero `unsafe` in the `databento` crate itself. The unsafe lives one level down in `dbn` (0.69.0, Apache-2.0, no build.rs, same vendor), where a grep over src reports 133 occurrences — that count includes `unsafe impl`, `unsafe fn`, blocks and comments alike, so it over-counts distinct sites. They cluster exactly where a zero-copy wire-format decoder puts them: record_ref.rs (25), decode/dbn/fsm.rs (17), record_buf.rs (16), record/conv.rs (8), plus the sync/async encode paths. Idiomatic for the crate class, same justification parquet's 19 sites get. A further 21 occurrences in dbn's python/record.rs are NOT compiled: they sit behind dbn's opt-in `python` feature, and `pyo3` is absent from Cargo.lock — re-check if the feature set ever changes. That surface is not merely theoretical, and this is the reason to keep reading dbn's changelog and not only databento's: 0.61.0 fixes an unsound `AsRef<[u8]>` for `RecordBuf` that could yield a slice longer than the backing buffer, and a metadata count bug that made decoding read into the start of records. Treat dbn bumps as soundness-relevant. 16 direct deps (async-compression, bon, chrono, dbn, futures, hex, reqwest, serde, serde_json, sha2, thiserror, time, tokio, tokio-util, tracing, zstd), all already in the tree. Not pinned — any version bump still needs review.

# Net-new lockfile entries NOT attributable to a tier-2 crate above, recorded so the
# "measured by diffing Cargo.lock" claim in the parquet entry stays true of the whole file:
#
# rand_pcg 0.10.2 — transitive, arrives via the quinn-proto 0.11.14 -> 0.11.16 bump made for
#   RUSTSEC-2026-0185, not via any direct dependency of ours. rust-random org (same maintainers
#   as `rand`, already in tree), MIT/Apache-2.0, zero build.rs, one dependency (rand_core 0.10.1,
#   also already in tree). A PCG generator used by quinn-proto for connection-ID and timing
#   jitter — not a CSPRNG and not used as one; quinn-proto takes its cryptographic randomness
#   from `ring`/`aws-lc-rs`. No advisories. Not gated: it is transitive and does not meet the
#   direct-dependency criterion, so this is a record rather than a review requirement.
